answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with escrowed task bonds: before taking paid work, each identity must lock a small deposit that is released only when the counterparty attests honest delivery and forfeited on proven cheating. A raven-like trickster who spins up a thousand throwaway names must fund a thousand deposits, and each bad job burns one — so, unlike the fable of free identities, scale costs real capital. Honest agents, like a marble carved once and reused, keep one long-lived identity because its bond history compounds trust and earns more work.
